messages.author: 6510ebbe3488de85
messages.subject: Transect Trapping
parts:
Hello All,

I am designing a study to look at the density of large fishes in an
expansive wetland adjacent to a canal. In addition to density, I am
interested in composition as it changes from near canal to central
wetland. There are several discrete openings in the canal where either
airboats or alligators have created small channels through the sawgrass
that probably serve as corridors for fish movement into the central areas
of the marsh.

I have researched several sampling methods and find that the trapping web
satisfies many of my conditions. However, within the program WebSim v.2 by
Paul Lukacs is also included an experimental approach called a Trapping
Transect. Given the potential linear arrangement of fishes occupying
corridors, perhaps a Trapping Transect approach would yield a more accurate
estimate of fish density than a Trapping Web?

I have found no studies referencing Trapping Transects, and the available
documentation on this method is not complete enough to base a study upon.
Is there anyone that can point me to documentation or examples where the
Trapping Transect has been used successfully?

--

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Transect Trapping
parts:
Mac, list,

Trapping transects are described, and an example given, in Chapter 9 of the
Advanced Distance Sampling book. If you don't have access to the book via a
local library, you can order a copy at 20% discount via
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.book/advanced.html

Another trapping-based approach, which makes use of recapture information, is
that of Murray Efford. Links to his papers and the software Density are at
http://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/services/software/density/

Hope this helps,

- Len

P.S.

> >Given the potential linear arrangement of fishes occupying
> >corridors, perhaps a Trapping Transect approach would yield a more accurate
> >estimate of fish density than a Trapping Web?

I was a bit puzzled by this -- you still have to lay the lines/points down at
random (/stratified random) within your study area (or strata) for valid
inference. However, other things being equal, trapping lines should have
lower variance than trapping webs in the same way that line transects are in
general more efficient than point transects.
